item: A MALLOC_ARENA_MAX named twice is read as a cap only on a glibc measured to apply the first copy
summary: glibc 2.39 applies the first accepted copy of a variable the starting environment names twice; the glibc of the ubuntu-26.04 runners applies the last (measured in CI: 3 then 1 kept 1 arena, -2 then 2 kept 2), and two tests that pinned 2.39 failed there. The reading now records which names the starting block repeats and claims a duplicated MALLOC_ARENA_MAX only on a version listed in _FIRST_COPY_WINS (glibc 2.39); elsewhere it reads as not known with the version named. A single copy reads as before on any glibc, and GLIBC_TUNABLES keeps being read in every copy (that held on 26.04 too). The real-allocator tests assert the measured rule on 2.39 and only one-of-the-two-copies elsewhere.
